hero.title: The Pandya Kingdom: Sangam Dynasty
hero.description: An exploration of the Pandyas, masters of the southern tip of India and patrons of the Sangam literature.

mockIntro.title: UPSC Level Mock Test
mockIntro.description: Test your grasp of Pandya history, Sangam literature, and trade networks with statement-based questions.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: Key historical phases of the Pandya rule in Ancient India.

cards.details: Mentioned by Megasthenes and Ashoka's edicts; centered in Korkai and Madurai.
A period of 'darkness' where Pandyas lost power to the Kalabhra invaders.
Kadungon restored the dynasty; rise of the First Pandyan Empire.

toolEvolution.title: Pandya Coinage Evolution
toolEvolution.description: The transformation of coins circulated in the Pandya kingdom, reflecting trade and cultural integration.

stages.name: Punch-Marked Coins
stages.desc: Silver punch-marked coins with fish symbol (royal emblem) and other symbols used for local trade.

stages.name: Fish & Conch
stages.desc: Copper coins featuring the Pandya royal fish emblem along with conch shells; also elephant and bull motifs.

stages.name: Roman Denarii Hoards
stages.desc: Massive hoards of Roman silver/coins found at Korkai and Madurai, evidence of the flourishing Indo-Roman trade through the Pandya ports.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Confusing the Early Sangam Pandyas with the Later Pandyas of the 13th century (Maravarman/Jatavarman).
Assuming the Pandya kingdom was purely land-based; ignore their immense naval focus and pearl trade supremacy.
Believing Sangam literature mentions specific dates for kings; it only provides genealogical context.

mnemonics.title: Mnemonics for Prelims
mnemonics.description: Remember the core elements of the Pandya legacy.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Centered in Tamraparni/Vaigai river basins
  • Capital: Madurai
  • Major Port: Korkai

Personalities

  • Nedunjeliyan: Famous Sangam King
  • Kadungon: Reviver of the dynasty
  • Ariyanpadi Kadanta: Epithet for victory

Core Structure of Pandya Society

  • Administration
    • Kingship was hereditary.
    • Divine status claimed by rulers.
    • Council of Ministers (Aimperunkulu).
  • Economy
    • Pearl Fishery: The backbone of prosperity.
    • Trade: Active relations with Roman Empire.
    • Revenue: 'Kadamai' (Land tax).
AspectDetail
SymbolFish (Kayal)
LiteraturePatronized Sangam assemblies
ReligionVedic & Jain/Buddhist influences

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following ports was the center of pearl fisheries for the Pandya kingdom?
practiceQuestions.sol: Korkai was the Pandya port famous for pearl fisheries on the Gulf of Mannar coast.

practiceQuestions.q: Who was the Pandya king associated with the execution of Kovalan in the Tamil epic Silappadikaram?
practiceQuestions.sol: Nedunjeliyan was the Pandya king who wrongfully executed Kovalan, leading to Kannagi's curse and the burning of Madurai.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Greek writer mentions a Pandya queen ruling the kingdom?
practiceQuestions.sol: Megasthenes, the Greek ambassador to the Mauryan court, mentions a Pandya queen named Pandaia in his work Indica.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the royal emblem of the Pandya dynasty?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Pandya royal emblem was the Fish (twin fish), the Chera emblem was the Bow and Arrow, and the Chola emblem was the Tiger.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Sangam Pandyas:
1. The Pandya kingdom is mentioned in Ashokan Rock Edict II.
2. Madurai was the capital of the Pandyas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Ashokan Rock Edict II mentions the Pandyas as independent kingdoms to the south. Madurai was the capital city.

practiceQuestions.q:
Assertion (A): The Pandyas were known for their maritime trade with the Roman Empire.
Reason (R): Korkai port was a major center for pearl fisheries that attracted Roman merchants.
Choose the correct answer:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
practiceQuestions.sol: Both A and R are true. The Pandya pearl trade through Korkai was extensively documented in Roman texts like Periplus of the Erythraean Sea, making R the correct explanation of A.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following literary works describes the city of Madurai under Pandya rule?
practiceQuestions.sol: Maduraikanchi, part of the Pattupattu (Ten Idylls), exclusively describes the city of Madurai, its walls, markets, and daily life under Pandya rule.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Cheras - Tiger
2. Cholas - Bow and Arrow
3. Pandyas - Fish
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
practiceQuestions.sol: Only one pair is correct. Pandyas - Fish is correct. Cheras = Bow and Arrow, Cholas = Tiger. The first two pairs are swapped.

practiceQuestions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Kingdom) - List-II (Capital)
A. Cheras - 1. Madurai
B. Cholas - 2. Vanji
C. Pandyas - 3. Uraiyur
practiceQuestions.sol: Correct matching: Cheras → Vanji, Cholas → Uraiyur, Pandyas → Madurai.

practiceQuestions.q: Fill in the blank: The third Sangam was held at ________ under the patronage of the Pandya kings.
practiceQuestions.sol: The third Sangam was held at Madurai under the patronage of the Pandya king Nedunjeliyan.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Roman text provides detailed accounts of the Pandya pearl trade?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea (1st century CE) provides detailed accounts of the Pandya pearl trade and Korkai port.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Pandya emblem was the Fish.
2. The Pandya early capital was Korkai.
3. Korkai was on the Malabar coast.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect - Korkai was on the Gulf of Mannar (south-east coast), not the Malabar (west) coast.

practiceQuestions.q:
Assertion (A): Megasthenes mentions a Pandya queen in his work Indica.
Reason (R): The Pandya kingdom had a matrilineal succession system.
Choose the correct answer:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
practiceQuestions.sol: Megasthenes does mention a Pandya queen named Pandaia. While this suggests possible matrilineal tendencies, the exact nature of Pandya succession is not definitively known, so R is not necessarily the correct explanation.

practiceQuestions.q: Who was the famous Pandya king who presided over the third Sangam?
practiceQuestions.sol: Nedunjeliyan (also known as Pandyan Nedunjeliyan) was the king under whom the third Sangam flourished at Madurai.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Korkai - Chera port
2. Muziris - Pandya port
3. Poompuhar - Chola port
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
practiceQuestions.sol: Only one pair is correct. Poompuhar = Chola port is correct. Korkai = Pandya port (not Chera). Muziris = Chera port (not Pandya).

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following was NOT a port of the Pandya kingdom?
practiceQuestions.sol: Muziris was a Chera port on the Malabar coast. Korkai, Saliyur, and Kolchoi (Greek name for Korkai) were Pandya ports.

practiceQuestions.q: The Korkai pearl fisheries were located in which water body?
practiceQuestions.sol: Korkai was located on the Gulf of Mannar, between India and Sri Lanka, which was rich in pearl oysters.

practiceQuestions.q:
Match the following:
A. Tolkappiyam - 1. Five Great Epics
B. Silappadikaram - 2. Tamil Grammar
C. Maduraikanchi - 3. Ten Idylls
practiceQuestions.sol: Tolkappiyam is the earliest Tamil grammar. Silappadikaram is one of the Five Great Tamil Epics. Maduraikanchi is part of the Ten Idylls (Pattupattu).

practiceQuestions.q: Which Pandya ruler revived the dynasty after the Kalabhra interregnum?
practiceQuestions.sol: Kadungon defeated the Kalabhras around the 6th century CE and revived the Pandya dynasty, marking the beginning of the Later Pandya phase.

practiceQuestions.q: Fill in the blank: The Pandya king ________ was the last powerful ruler before the invasion of Malik Kafur.
practiceQuestions.sol: Maravarman Kulasekhara was the last great Pandya ruler before Malik Kafur's invasion in 1310-11 CE.

practiceQuestions.q:
Assertion (A): The Pandya kingdom had a strong naval presence.
Reason (R): Pearl fishing and maritime trade were central to the Pandya economy.
Choose the correct answer:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
practiceQuestions.sol: Both A and R are true. The Pandya economy depended heavily on pearl fishing and maritime trade with Rome, requiring a strong naval presence to protect these interests.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following Tamil works was produced under the patronage of the third Sangam at Madurai?
practiceQuestions.sol: Tolkappiyam, the earliest Tamil grammar, was traditionally composed during the third Sangam at Madurai under Pandya patronage.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Pandyas:
1. They used the fish as their royal emblem on coins.
2. They were mentioned in Ashokan inscriptions.
3. Megasthenes wrote exclusively about Pandya military campaigns.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is incorrect - Megasthenes mentioned a Pandya queen ruling the kingdom, not military campaigns.

practiceQuestions.q: To which Sangam kingdom does the port of Korkai belong?
practiceQuestions.sol: Korkai was the chief port of the Pandya kingdom on the Gulf of Mannar, famous for pearl fisheries.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. First Sangam - Kapatapuram
2. Second Sangam - Ten Madurai
3. Third Sangam - Madurai
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
practiceQuestions.sol: Only one pair is correct. Third Sangam at Madurai is correct. The First Sangam was at Ten Madurai (now submerged), and the Second Sangam was at Kapatapuram.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the inland capital of the Pandya kingdom connected to Korkai by river routes?
practiceQuestions.sol: Madurai was the inland capital and center of commerce, connected to the port of Korkai by river routes.

practiceQuestions.q: Which ancient text mentions that ships from Egypt reached Pandya ports in about 40 days?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea mentions that ships would reach the Pandya ports from Egypt in about 40 days using the monsoon winds (Hippalus).

practiceQuestions.q:
Assertion (A): The Pandyas patronized the three Tamil Sangams.
Reason (R): The Pandyas were great patrons of Tamil literature and culture.
Choose the correct answer:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
practiceQuestions.sol: Both A and R are true. The Pandya kings were renowned patrons of Tamil literature, hosting all three Sangam assemblies at their capitals, making R the correct explanation.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Pandya ruler built the famous Meenakshi Amman Temple gopurams?
practiceQuestions.sol: Jatavarman Sundara Pandya, at the peak of Later Pandya power in the 13th century, built the famous Meenakshi Amman Temple gopurams at Madurai.

practiceQuestions.q:
Match the following:
A. Roman gold coins - 1. Korkai
B. Pearl fishery - 2. Madurai
C. Third Sangam - 3. Pandya hoards
practiceQuestions.sol: Roman gold coin hoards were found in Pandya territory (A-3). Korkai was the pearl fishery center (B-1). The Third Sangam was held at Madurai (C-2).

practiceQuestions.q: Who wrote the oldest surviving Tamil grammar text produced under Pandya patronage?
practiceQuestions.sol: Tolkappiyam was written by Tolkappiyar, a disciple of the sage Agastya, during the third Sangam at Madurai.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following:
1. Pandya coins featured the fish emblem.
2. Pandya coins featured the tiger emblem.
3. Pandya coins featured the bow and arrow.
Which of the above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Pandya coins featured the fish emblem. The tiger was the Chola emblem and the bow and arrow was the Chera emblem.

practiceQuestions.q: Fill in the blank: The Greek ambassador ________ mentioned the Pandya queen in his work Indica.
practiceQuestions.sol: Megasthenes, the Greek ambassador to Chandragupta Maurya's court, mentioned a Pandya queen named Pandaia in his work Indica.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following items was a major export from the Pandya kingdom to the Roman Empire?
practiceQuestions.sol: Pearls from Korkai were the most prized export from the Pandya kingdom to the Roman Empire. Romans imported gold, coral, glassware, and wine from Rome.

practiceQuestions.q:
Assertion (A): The Later Pandyas were different from the Sangam Pandyas.
Reason (R): The Later Pandyas adopted different titles like 'Maravarman' and ruled in a different political context.
Choose the correct answer:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
practiceQuestions.sol: Both A and R are true. The Later Pandyas (post-6th century CE) adopted distinctive titles like Maravarman and Jatavarman and ruled in a different geopolitical context than the Sangam-era Pandyas.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Sangam work exclusively describes Madurai city under Pandya rule?
practiceQuestions.sol: Maduraikanchi is part of the Pattupattu (Ten Idylls) and exclusively describes the city of Madurai under Pandya rule.

practiceQuestions.q: In which century did Malik Kafur invade the Pandya kingdom?
practiceQuestions.sol: Malik Kafur, the general of Alauddin Khalji, invaded the Pandya kingdom in 1310-11 CE, i.e., in the early 14th century.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Pandyas controlled the southernmost tip of India.
2. The Vaigai river basin was the agricultural lifeline of the Pandyas.
3. The Pandyas had no overseas trade connections.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Pandyas controlled the southern tip of India and centered around the Vaigai basin. Statement 3 is incorrect as they had extensive Roman trade.

practiceQuestions.q: What was the early capital of the Pandyas before Madurai?
practiceQuestions.sol: Korkai served as the early capital of the Pandyas before they moved their capital inland to Madurai.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following was NOT an item imported by the Pandyas from the Roman Empire?
practiceQuestions.sol: Pearls and muslin were EXPORTED from the Pandyas to Rome, not imported. Gold coins, coral, glass, wine, and copper were imported from Rome.

practiceQuestions.q:
Match the following:
A. Nedunjeliyan - 1. Revived Pandya dynasty
B. Kadungon - 2. Third Sangam patron
C. Jatavarman Sundara - 3. Meenakshi temple builder
practiceQuestions.sol: Nedunjeliyan presided over the third Sangam (A-2). Kadungon revived the dynasty (B-1). Jatavarman Sundara built the Meenakshi temple gopurams (C-3).

practiceQuestions.q: Fill in the blank: The Pandya kingdom was mentioned in Ashokan ________.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Pandyas were mentioned as independent kingdoms in Ashokan Major Rock Edict II, along with the Cheras, Cholas, and Satyaputras.

practiceQuestions.q: Which dynasty was also known as 'Keralaputras' in Ashokan inscriptions?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Cheras were referred to as 'Keralaputras' in Ashokan inscriptions. The Pandyas were simply referred to as 'Pandyas'.

practiceQuestions.q:
Assertion (A): The Pandyas declined after the Kalabhra interregnum.
Reason (R): The Kalabhras were defeated by Kadungon who revived the Pandya dynasty.
Choose the correct answer:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are true but the revival happened later. The Kalabhra interregnum caused the decline, but Kadungon's revival occurred after a long gap.

practiceQuestions.q: Which ocean route was used by Roman ships to reach Pandya ports?
practiceQuestions.sol: Roman ships used the monsoon winds (discovered by Hippalus) to sail directly across the Indian Ocean to reach Pandya ports like Korkai.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following:
1. The Pandyas issued punch-marked coins.
2. The Pandyas issued Roman-style coins.
3. The Pandyas hoarded Roman denarii.
Which of the above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three are correct. Pandyas issued their own punch-marked coins with fish symbols, later coins with the fish emblem, and massive hoards of Roman coins have been found at Korkai and Madurai.

practiceQuestions.q: Which modern Indian state was the core region of the Pandya kingdom?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Pandya kingdom was centered in the southern part of modern-day Tamil Nadu, with Madurai as its capital.

practiceQuestions.q:
Match the following:
A. Ettutogai - 1. Eight Anthologies
B. Pattupattu - 2. Ten Idylls
C. Silappadikaram - 3. Tamil Epic
practiceQuestions.sol: Ettutogai means Eight Anthologies. Pattupattu means Ten Idylls. Silappadikaram is a Tamil epic composed by Ilango Adigal.

practiceQuestions.q: Fill in the blank: Pliny the Elder complained about the drain of Roman gold due to the import of Indian ________ from the Pandya kingdom.
practiceQuestions.sol: Pliny the Elder specifically complained about the drain of Roman gold due to the import of Indian pearls, which were primarily sourced from the Pandya kingdom's Korkai fisheries.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following statements about Pandya coinage is INCORRECT?
opts: Pandya coins featured the fish emblem
Pandya coins featured the tiger emblem
Pandya coins included punch-marked silver coins
Pandya coins included copper coins with conch motifs
practiceQuestions.sol: The tiger was the emblem of the Cholas, not the Pandyas. The Pandya emblem was the fish (or twin fish).

practiceQuestions.q: The Pandya kingdom's control over pearl fisheries gave them a monopoly in which ancient industry?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Pandyas had a virtual monopoly on pearl harvesting in the ancient world through their control of the Gulf of Mannar pearl banks.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The First Sangam was held at Ten Madurai.
2. The Second Sangam was held at Kapatapuram.
3. The Third Sangam was held at Madurai.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: All three statements are correct as per Tamil tradition. All three Sangams were held under Pandya patronage at different locations.

practiceQuestions.q: Which famous Tamil epic involves the Pandya king Nedunjeliyan executing Kovalan?
practiceQuestions.sol: Silappadikaram, written by Ilango Adigal, narrates the story of Kovalan's wrongful execution by the Pandya king Nedunjeliyan.

practiceQuestions.q:
Assertion (A): The Pandyas were one of the three crowned kings (Muvendar) of ancient South India.
Reason (R): The Muvendar included the Cheras, Cholas, and Pandyas.
Choose the correct answer:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
practiceQuestions.sol: Both A and R are true. The Pandyas were indeed one of the Muvendar (three crowned kings) along with the Cheras and Cholas, making R the correct explanation.

mockTestQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Sangam Pandyas:
1. Their capital was Uraiyur.
2. The fish was their royal emblem.
3. Korkai was their major port.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mockTestQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: Uraiyur was the Chola capital. The Pandya capital was Madurai. Statements 2 and 3 are correct.

mockTestQuestions.q: With reference to the ancient Tamil Sangam, which of the following was NOT held under Pandya patronage?
mockTestQuestions.sol: The Sangam at Vanji was associated with the Cheras, not the Pandyas. All three traditional Sangams were held under Pandya patronage.
